title: Understanding the Logistic Regression Equation
text: In logistic regression, the decision boundary is derived from the equation of the form: \( $$\theta_0$$ + $$\theta_1 X_1$$ + $$\theta_2 X_2$$ $$=$$ $$0$$ \). Here, \( $$\theta$$ \) represents the parameter vector. Can you identify the values of \( $$\theta_0$$ \), \( $$\theta_1$$ \), and \( $$\theta_2$$ \) from the given parameter vector?

title: Setting the Probability Threshold
text: The decision boundary is where the probability of preferring Kendrick is $$0.5$$. In logistic regression, this corresponds to the point where the linear combination of features equals zero. How does this relate to the equation \( $$\theta_0$$ + $$\theta_1 X_1$$ + $$\theta_2 X_2$$ $$=$$ $$0$$ \)?

title: Identify the Parameters
text: What are the values of \( $$\theta_0$$ \), \( $$\theta_1$$ \), and \( $$\theta_2$$ \) in the parameter vector \( $$\theta=(-2, 2, 1)$$ \)?
